newsitem.title: USA: American Power sued by competitor.
newsitem.headline: American Power sued by competitor.

text.p: Tripp Lite, a division of Trippe Manufacturing Co, on Wednesday said it filed a lawsuit seeking to undo the merger of American Power Conversion Corp and System Enhancement Corp.

The suit, filed on Monday in the U.S. District Court in Chicago, alleges American Power and System Enhancement engaged in restraint of trade and antitrust activity. It also accuses System Enhancement of breaching a contract with Tripp Lite.

"It is our opinion, and that of counsel, that (American Power's) recent acquisition of (System Enhancement) is predatory in nature and, therefore, patently unfair," Keelin Wyman, vice president of Tripp Lite marketing, said in a statement. "We are filing suit to protect our current as well as future interests."
American Power acquired System Enhancement in February for $13 mllion in American Power shares.
American Power said in a statement that it thought the lawsuit was without merit and planned to mount a vigorous defense.
It also said the suit should not have a material adverse effect on the company's financial position or results of operations and liquidity.
"This matter has no impact on APC's current financial guidance for the second quarter or fiscal 1997," said Donald Muir, the company's chief financial officer.
Tripp Lite and American Power both provide power protection products used in the computer and telecommunications industries.
Systems Enhancement develops and markets power management software for the uninterruptible power supply (UPS) industry.
